0 jobs! Because with 2048 connections and S=256 slots, each connection appears every 2048 packets, so windows never fill (W=16) — each connection's slot gets overwritten by other connections. Let me adjust: use fewer connections so windows fill. Let me use nconn = 200 or so, and slots large enough.

Let me modify: make the stress test use connections = min(2048, ...) but packets cycling over a small set so windows fill. Actually to get worst case CNN load I want every packet to be "sent" — need full windows and enough credit and pending capacity.

Let me set nconn=64 (each conn appears every 64 packets), idle_timeout large, W=16. Then each connection's window fills. With rate_num=1e6 per tick and rate_den=1, credit is plentiful. pending_capacity=512 and service=1 with 4 lanes: jobs complete quickly (done = start+1, and each packet time increments by 1 → jobs finish).

Let me parametrize the stress script.

arguments.command:
cd /workspace && python3 - << 'EOF'
p='tmp/stress.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('mode = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "full"',
            'mode = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "full"\nnconn = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 2048')
s=s.replace('nconn = 2048\nids','ids')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
python3 tmp/stress.py 7 20000 full 64 > tmp/big.json && ls -l tmp/big.json && time python3 submission/main.py < tmp/big.json > tmp/big_out.json && ls -l tmp/big_out.json && python3 -c "
import json; d=json.load(open('tmp/big_out.json')); print('packets',len(d['packets']),'jobs',len(d['jobs']));
from collections import Counter; print(Counter(p['decision'] for p in d['packets'])); print(Counter(j['status'] for j in d['jobs']))"
